# Exact discrete simplex-law obstruction to the probability-only cubic

## Statement and scope

For a probability law X on the simplex Δ₂={x≥0:Σx_i=1}, define

    φ_i(X)=inf{t/sqrt(P(X_i≤t)): t>0, P(X_i≤t)>0}.

The assertion Σφ_i²+2φ₁φ₂φ₃≤1 for every such law is false. The archived exact coupling certificate gives an explicit finite rational counterexample with

    (φ₁,φ₂,φ₃)=(200,100,100)/273,
    Σφ_i²+2φ₁φ₂φ₃−1=33583/20346417>0.

This says nothing against the separately proved uniform-triangle stochastic theorem or an ordinary uniform-convex-body cubic. The missing hypothesis is actual uniform convex geometry. This note is a direct discrete promotion of the already archived beta-coupling obstruction, not a new numerical construction.

## Finite data and exact construction

Use `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/beta_coupling_exact_certificate_root.json`, whose 399 positive rational weights m(i,j,k), with 0≤i,j,k<200, satisfy

    Σm=1,
    Σ_{j,k}m(i,j,k)=(2i+1)/40000,
    Σ_{i,k}m(i,l,k)+Σ_{i,j}m(i,j,l)=2(2l+1)/40000,
    2(i+1)+(j+1)+(k+1)≤546.

The second displayed marginal identity means that the last two coordinate marginals have the stated sum; they need not individually equal it. Select a triple with probability m(i,j,k), then independently interchange its last two entries with probability 1/2. Let

    U=((i+1)/200,(j+1)/200,(k+1)/200).

Each U-coordinate has exact atom mass (2l+1)/40000 at (l+1)/200. Consequently, for every real t≥0,

    P(U_q≤t)≤t²,

because at each grid endpoint l/200 the CDF is l²/40000, and between grid endpoints it is constant. For t≥1 this is also immediate. The support bound is

    2U₁+U₂+U₃≤273/100.

Put c=(200,100,100)/273, Z_q=c_q U_q, and

    X=(1−Z₂−Z₃,Z₂,Z₃).

Then X lies in Δ₂ and X₁≥Z₁. Thus for every t>0,

    P(X_q≤t)≤P(Z_q≤t)≤t²/c_q²,

where for q=2,3 the first inequality is equality. Hence φ_q(X)≥c_q. This already proves failure of the cubic, which is coordinatewise increasing on the nonnegative orthant.

The exact finite check gives equality of all capacities. Coordinates 2 and 3 attain it at every positive grid endpoint, in particular at t=100/273 with CDF 1. Coordinate 1 attains it at t=6/13, where its CDF is 3969/10000; indeed

    (6/13)²/(3969/10000)=40000/74529=(200/273)².

Combining coincident atoms leaves 678 rational atoms on Δ₂. The law is defined completely by the archived rational data and the displayed deterministic map and symmetrization.

## Independent exact verification

`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_discrete_simplex_capacity_cubic_obstruction_two_sided.py` reads the rational JSON directly and checks positivity, total mass, all support inequalities, all three marginal identities after symmetrization, every promoted simplex atom, every CDF at each marginal atom, all three exact capacity squares, and the rational cubic excess. Between successive atoms t²/F(t) increases, so checking atom thresholds is sufficient for the exact capacity computation.

Result: 3,586 exact rational checks PASS. No optimization or floating-point solver is used in this verifier. The branch seeking a probability-only universal cubic is blocked by this certificate; any continuation must retain additional uniform convex-body constraints.
